simple.meaning: אַשָּׁף (ʼashshâph) is a Hebrew object word meaning “astrologer.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Daniel 2:10. The surrounding context includes family, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַשָּׁף (H826) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אַשָּׁף (ʼashshâph) / H826 is traced through Daniel 2:10, Daniel 2:27, Daniel 4:4, Daniel 5:7 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The Chaldeans answered before the king, and said, “There is not a man on the earth who can show the king’s matter, because no king, lord, or ruler, has asked such a thing of any magician, or enchanter, or Chaldean.

timeline.evidenceText: The Chaldeans answered before the king, and said, “There is not a man on the earth who can show the king’s matter, because no king, lord, or ruler, has asked such a thing of any magician, or enchanter, or Chaldean.
Daniel answered before the king, and said, “The secret which the king has demanded can’t be shown to the king by wise men, enchanters, magicians, or soothsayers;
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at rest in my house, and flourishing in my palace.

The king cried aloud to bring in the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers. The king spoke and said to the wise men of Babylon, “Whoever reads this writing, and shows me its interpretation, shall be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold about his neck, and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.”

There is a man in your kingdom, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods; and in the days of your father light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, were found in him. The king Nebuchadnezzar your father, yes, the king, your father, made him master of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and soothsayers;
Now the wise men, the enchanters, have been brought in before me, that they should read this writing, and make known to me its interpretation; but they could not show the interpretation of the thing.

definitions.full: H826. ashaph אָשַׁף (K§ a) noun masculine conjurer, enchanter (probably Babylonian Loan-word; so Biblical Hebrew אַשָּׁף ); — absolute ׳א Dan 2:10 ; plural absolute אָֽשְׁפִין 2:27 ; 5:11 , emphatic אָֽשְׁפַיָא 4:4 ; 5:7 , 15 .
